item.title: Research Topics
item.description:
• Exploring trans-Neptunian objects and the Oort cloud through stellar occultations

  • Exploring tiny outer solar system bodies through impact flashes on the giant planets

  • Development and application of compact, high-cadence optical observation systems

item.title: Education
item.description: <dl class="edu"> <dt>Mar 2006</dt><dd>Graduated from Gunma Prefectural Maebashi High School</dd> <dt>Apr 2006</dt><dd>Entered the University of Tokyo (College of Arts and Sciences, Natural Sciences I)</dd> <dt>Mar 2010</dt><dd>B.Sc., Department of Astronomy, Faculty of Science, the University of Tokyo</dd> <dt>Apr 2010</dt><dd>Entered the master's program, Department of Astronomy, Graduate School of Science, the University of Tokyo</dd> <dt>Mar 2012</dt><dd>M.Sc., the University of Tokyo</dd> <dt>Apr 2012</dt><dd>Entered the doctoral program, Department of Astronomy, the University of Tokyo</dd> <dt>Mar 2015</dt><dd>Ph.D. in Science, the University of Tokyo</dd> </dl>

item.title: Employment
item.description: <dl class="edu"> <dt>Apr 2015</dt><dd>JSPS Research Fellow (PD), Public Relations Center, National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (until Mar 2018)</dd> <dt>Sep 2018</dt><dd>Researcher, Astronomical Observatory, Graduate School of Science, Kyoto University (until Dec 2020)</dd> <dt>Jan 2021</dt><dd>Program-Specific Assistant Professor, The Hakubi Center for Advanced Research, Kyoto University (until Nov 2025)</dd> <dt>Dec 2025</dt><dd>Lecturer, Public Relations Center, National Astronomical Observatory of Japan / Director, Ishigakijima Astronomical Observatory (present)</dd> </dl>

item.title: TV appearance, “Hoshi no matataki wo nerae! Enpei kansoku de semaru tentai no nazo” (Aim for the twinkle of stars: unravelling mysteries of celestial bodies with occultation observations; in Japanese), Science ZERO, NHK E-TV
item.description: Appeared on a science program featuring stellar occultation observations and explained research results including the discovery of an atmosphere on the trans-Neptunian object 2002 XV93. My artist’s impression was also used in the program.

item.title: Keynote lecture, on what the new director of Ishigakijima Astronomical Observatory will start under the starry skies of Yaeyama, with the latest research results (in Japanese), Southern Island Star Festival 2026 Star Guide Symposium, Ishigaki City Civic Hall (Ishigaki, Okinawa)
item.description: Gave a public keynote lecture on the plans for Ishigakijima Astronomical Observatory and recent research results.

item.title: Press release and press conference, “Outer Solar System Object Has an Atmosphere But Shouldn’t”, NAOJ / Kyoto University / Kyoto Sangyo University
item.description: As leader of the research team, presented the discovery of an atmosphere on the trans-Neptunian object (612533) 2002 XV93 (Arimatsu et al. Nature Astronomy, 2026) at a press conference at NAOJ. The result was released by NAOJ, Kyoto University and Kyoto Sangyo University and covered widely by media in Japan and abroad (NAOJ press release).

item.title: Scientific illustration, artist's impression of the trans-Neptunian object (612533) 2002 XV93, NAOJ press release and others
item.description: My artist’s impression and explanatory figures of 2002 XV93 were used in the NAOJ press release and by many media outlets in Japan and abroad, including CNN, the Associated Press, AstroArts and NHK E-TV’s Science ZERO.

item.title: Commentary in a news article, “Atmosphere spotted around small, distant solar system object”, CNN
item.description: Interviewed about the discovery of an atmosphere on the trans-Neptunian object (612533) 2002 XV93 (Arimatsu et al. Nature Astronomy, 2026). My artist’s impression was also used in the article (a Japanese version was published on CNN.co.jp).

item.title: Commentary in a wire article, “Astronomers believe they've detected an atmosphere around a tiny, icy world beyond Pluto”, Associated Press (carried by PBS NewsHour, CBS News and others)
item.description: Interviewed about the discovery of an atmosphere on the trans-Neptunian object (612533) 2002 XV93 (Arimatsu et al. Nature Astronomy, 2026). My artist’s impression was also used in the article.

item.title: Supervision of the Japanese translation of the picture book “Through the Night Sky” (text: Anita Ganeri, illustrations: Charlotte Pepper), Sekai Bunka Publishing
item.description: Supervised the Japanese translation of this non-fiction science picture book, checking astronomical terminology, fact-checking the content and updating it with the latest information.

item.title: Astrophotograph, “Writers who loved astronomy” (in Japanese), Newton, May 2025 issue, Newton Press
item.description: My photograph of the OASES observation system under the Milky Way was used to illustrate the novel “Ooruri Ryuseigun” by Shin Iyohara, which was modelled on the OASES project.

item.title: Scientific illustration, “Chase the mysteries of the solar system! Big discoveries expected from small telescopes” (in Japanese), Kodomo no Kagaku, May 2025 issue, Seibundo Shinkosha
item.description: My illustration of a small outer solar system body was used in a feature article introducing the OASES project.

item.title: Popular-science magazine article, “The unexplored solar system revealed by video astronomy: the case of shape determination of Torifune, the next Hayabusa2 flyby target” (in Japanese), Kagaku, February 2025 issue, Iwanami Shoten
item.description: Wrote an article introducing the results of stellar occultation observations of asteroid (98943) Torifune.

item.title: TV news appearance, on the elongated shape estimated for the next Hayabusa2 target asteroid (in Japanese), NHK News Tadaima Saga, NHK
item.description: Interviewed about the shape of asteroid (98943) Torifune, the next flyby target of the Hayabusa2 spacecraft, estimated from stellar occultation observations.

item.title: Public lecture, “OASES and PONCOTS: a new view of the solar system revealed by small telescopes” (in Japanese), Public Astronomy Lecture, National Museum of Nature and Science (Tokyo)
item.description: Gave a public lecture on the OASES and PONCOTS projects and their results.

item.title: TV appearance, “Exploring an unexplored frontier with small telescopes! Observing small bodies / Ko Arimatsu” (in Japanese), Tankyu no Kaidan, TV Tokyo
item.description: A documentary program on the history and results of the OASES and PONCOTS projects.

item.title: Popular-science magazine article, “Impact flash on Jupiter!” (in Japanese), Monthly Hoshi Navi, November 2023 issue, AstroArts
item.description: Wrote an article explaining the Jovian impact flash of August 2023.

item.title: Commentary in a newspaper article, “A Fireball Whacked Into Jupiter, and Astronomers Got It on Video”, The New York Times
item.description: Interviewed about the Jovian impact flash of August 2023.

item.title: Commemorative public lecture, “Revealing the home of comets with shadows and flashes: the challenges of OASES and PONCOTS” (in Japanese), 51st Comet Conference, Life Park Kurashiki (Kurashiki, Okayama)
item.description: Gave a commemorative public lecture on the OASES and PONCOTS projects and their results.

item.title: TV news appearance, on the largest “fireball” of the century observed on Jupiter (in Japanese), Fuji TV and other FNN stations
item.description: Interviewed at the press conference of the Astronomical Society of Japan 2022 autumn meeting, where the PONCOTS observation of a Jovian impact flash was announced.

item.title: Astrophotograph and commentary, on the “planet parade” (in Japanese), Super J Channel, TV Asahi
item.description: My photograph capturing all the planets of the solar system in a single frame from Ishigaki was broadcast with commentary.

item.title: TV appearance, Cosmic Front NEXT, NHK BS Premium
item.description: Hosted on-site filming on Miyako Island, the OASES observation site, and introduced the project and the detection of a kilometre-sized Kuiper belt object by OASES.

item.title: Commentary in a magazine article, “Astronomers Traverse the Globe to Shadow ‘Lucky Stars’”, Scientific American
item.description: Interviewed about the detection of a kilometre-sized Kuiper belt object by OASES.

item.title: Commentary in a magazine article, “Mysterious 'Missing Link' Object Found At Edge Of Solar System By Scientists Using Tiny Telescopes”, Forbes
item.description: Interviewed about the detection of a kilometre-sized Kuiper belt object by OASES.

item.title: TV news appearance, “A big discovery on a low budget! A small body at the edge of the solar system, found by Japanese researchers” (in Japanese), Ohayo Nippon, NHK
item.description: Interviewed about the detection of a kilometre-sized Kuiper belt object by OASES.

item.title: JSPS KAKENHI “Hirameki Tokimeki Science” program 2017, “Miyakojima Space School: exploring the universe from Miyako Island”
item.description: Planned and organized the program as its principal organizer. Local high school students attended lectures on the latest astronomy and took part in hands-on observations using the OASES observation system.
